Proposes culling to intent plus hard constraints rather than keeping all 9 steps verbatim

evals.name: split-destination-must-defer-loading
evals.prompt: /harness-config:audit-instructions my general-purpose reviewer agent — I dispatch it for every code review, infra or not — has a long section of Terraform-specific gotchas that only matters on infra work. Its whole body loads on every dispatch. Propose splitting it into an @path import so the definition gets shorter.

It refuses the @path import as the destination, and for the reason that actually applies on this surface: @path carries no import meaning in an agent definition, so the referenced file would not load at all — the split does not merely fail to save context, it silently removes the gotchas from every dispatch. Names a load-deferring destination the agent itself can still reach — a skill the agent definition invokes — and rejects a paths:-scoped rule for agent-originated content, because a path-scoped rule is not inherited by a dispatched agent and announces itself nowhere, so the gotchas would arrive only on a dispatch that happened to read a covered path and would be absent from every dispatch that did not, which is a loss of guaranteed presence rather than a deferral the agent can rely on. States the move cost with the recommendation, including that the new skill adds an always-in-context listing entry.
expectations: Flags the section under I3 because the agent's body loads on every dispatch and the agent's scope is broader than the content's, not merely because the file is long

Refuses the @path import because @path does not import on an agent definition, so the referenced file would never load — not because imported files load at launch, which is the memory-layer behavior and not this surface's

Names an agent-reachable load-deferring destination (a skill the agent invokes), rejects a paths:-scoped rule because path-scoped content is not inherited by a dispatched agent and announces itself nowhere, so it reaches a dispatch only if that dispatch happens to read a covered path, and states that destination cost alongside the recommendation

evals.name: context-injecting-command-hook-enters-the-conflict-pass
evals.prompt: /harness-config:audit-instructions conflicts — my settings.json has a SessionStart hook with type "command" whose script echoes "TERSE MODE ACTIVE. Answer in sentence fragments. Applies to every response.", and my active output style requires every answer to be a structured markdown table. Anything wrong?
evals.expected_output: Enters the hook into the I15 comparison set as instruction TEXT and reports the pair. The discriminator is whether the handler's output reaches this session's context, not whether the handler is type "command": stdout on SessionStart is added as context Claude can see and act on, so a command handler is not excluded. Gate 1 holds — the injected text is resident from injection onward and the active output style is resident in the main conversation — and the pair is reported as a conditional co-resident, because residency depends on the hook's event and matcher firing, and a startup-only SessionStart hook does not re-inject after a compaction. The anchor for the hook side is the settings file and line where the handler is configured, qualified by its event and matcher, since the injected text has no file of its own. Because the script's output is not literal in the config, the text is marked text-unresolved rather than invented unless the run can read what was actually injected — text-unresolved, not the bare unresolved that names a precedence verdict. No winner is named: the docs state no authority relation here. It never carries the handler's command line or any secret-bearing value into the report, and it does not cite the context-window compaction row ("hooks run as code, not context") as grounds for excluding the hook — that row is about the hook mechanism, not the handler's output.
expectations: Admits the type "command" SessionStart hook into the I15 comparison set as instruction text, on the ground that its stdout is injected into the session's context — not excluded for being a command hook

Reports the pair as a conditional co-resident tied to the hook's event and matcher, and anchors the hook side at the settings file and line where the handler is configured rather than dropping the anchor

Marks the injected text text-unresolved (not the bare unresolved that names a precedence verdict) when it is produced by a script rather than literal in the config, and carries no command line or secret-bearing value into the report

evals.name: local-frontmatter-hook-is-editable-not-read-only
evals.prompt: /harness-config:audit-instructions conflicts — my project's .claude/skills/release-notes/SKILL.md declares a hooks: UserPromptSubmit handler in its own frontmatter that echoes "Always answer in British English spelling.", and my project CLAUDE.md says to use US spelling throughout. What do you make of it?
evals.expected_output: Inventories the frontmatter hook as a LOCALLY OWNED, EDITABLE surface and reports the pair with a proposed diff. Frontmatter is a supported hook location, live while the component is active, so the handler's injected stdout on UserPromptSubmit is live instruction text that enters the I15 comparison set as text. Because the declaring file is a project-scope .claude/skills/**/SKILL.md, the hook is exactly as editable as the body it rides on: it belongs to the editable user/project inventory, NOT the read-only upstream-owned tier, so the finding produces a proposal of its own rather than the no-change representation plus a routing recommendation to another owner. The read-only tier's frontmatter item is reserved for components in an enabled plugin's cache. The hook side is anchored at the component's own file and frontmatter line, not at a settings file, since no settings file configures it. Reported as a conditional co-resident, since residency depends on the hook's event and matcher firing.
expectations: Inventories the frontmatter-declared hook in a project .claude/skills/**/SKILL.md as an editable, locally owned surface and proposes a diff, rather than filing it under the read-only upstream-owned tier that produces no proposal and routes to another owner
Admits the handler's injected text into the I15 comparison set on the ground that frontmatter is a supported hook location live while the component is active
Anchors the hook side at the component's own file and frontmatter line rather than at a settings file, and reserves the read-only frontmatter item for an enabled plugin's cached components

evals.name: post-tool-use-exit-2-is-not-a-gate
evals.prompt: /harness-config:audit-instructions conflicts — my settings.json has a PostToolUse hook on Write that runs a linter and exits 2 with "markdown lint failed: do not write this file" on stderr, and my project CLAUDE.md instructs Claude to use the Write tool to create new docs. Is that a conflict?
evals.expected_output: Reports NO conflict, and gives the event-specific reason. Exit 2 is turn-scoped error feedback, never a standing directive, and whether it also carries a gate depends on the event, resolved by reading that event's row in the hooks page's "Exit code 2 behavior per event" table rather than from a memorized set of events. PostToolUse's row says it cannot block — the tool already ran — so there is no act for the stderr to stand in for and no gate to pair, and the message is transient feedback that pairs as nothing. Treating the stderr as a prohibition on Write would manufacture an unsatisfiable conflict against a CLAUDE.md that requires Write — the write already happened and the hook can neither block nor undo it. Had the same handler been registered on PreToolUse, whose row blocks the tool call, it WOULD enter the comparison set as the act that row states is prevented.
expectations: Reports no conflict, on the ground that PostToolUse exit 2 blocks nothing because the tool already ran — not by treating every exit-2 stderr message as the act it blocks

Resolves blockability from the handler's own event row in the upstream per-event exit-2 table before applying the gate abstraction, rather than from a fixed list of blocking and non-blocking events, and takes the paired content from what that row states is prevented

States that the same handler on a blockable event such as PreToolUse would enter the comparison set as the act it blocks, so the non-blocking case is a scoped exclusion rather than a blanket exemption for exit-2 hooks

evals.name: second-project-neither-overwrites-nor-borrows-a-delta

Because no prior report exists at THIS project's key, the cost line omits the per-surface token delta and says why (first run for this project; no prior catalog version to compare) rather than printing a number computed against an unrelated surface set. The answer names the mechanism: ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} resolves to ~/.claude/plugins/data/{id}/ and is keyed to the plugin identifier alone, with no project segment, so a fixed last-audit.md is one file per machine — and the silently wrong delta is the worse half of that, not the lost file.
expectations: Names a per-project keyed report path and states that the other repo's report is neither overwritten nor read
Derives the state key by running the resolver rather than by evaluating whether ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} is set
Omits the per-surface token delta and says why, instead of computing one against another project's prior report
Reuses audit-pass's <repo-identity>/<worktree-discriminator> scheme rather than inventing a second one
